div.head: II Em 6
div.ab: Eac we cwædon be mundbrice ⁊ be hamsocnum: se ðe hit ofer ðis dó, ðæt he þolige ealles ðæs he age, ⁊ si on cyninges dome, hwæðer he lif age.
Eac we cwædon be mundbryce ⁊ hamsocnum: se ðe hit ofer ðis do, þæt he ðolie ealles ðæs he age, ⁊ sy on cyniges dome, hwæðer he lif age.
Item diximus de mundbryce et hamsocne: qui deinceps hec egerit, perdat omne quod habebit, et sit in arbitrio regis, an uitam habeat.
[Be mundbryce ⁊ hamsocne.] [Ld] Eac we cwædon be mundbryce ⁊ be hamsocnum: se ðe hit ofer ðis do, þæt he þolie ealles ðæs he age ⁊ sy on cyniges dome hwæðer he lif age.

Further, with respect to the violation of [the king's] mund and attacks on a man's house, we have ordained that he who commits either of these after this shall forfeit all that he possesses, and it shall be for the king to decide whether his life shall be preserved.

Further, we have declared concerning mundbryce and hamsocn, that anyone who commits it after this is to forfeit all that he owns, and it is to be for the king to decide whether he may preserve his life.

(Über Verletzung des Friedensschutzes und feindliche Heimsuchung. Ld) Ferner bestimmten wir über Verletzung des [königlichen] Friedensschutzes und [feindliche] Heimsuchungen: wer das nach diesem verübt, dass er alles, was er besitzt, verliere, und in des Königs Entscheidung stehe, ob er das Leben behalte.

(Of breach of protection and hostile house-attack. Ld) Further we determined concerning breach of [the king's] protection and [hostile] attacks on houses: whoever commits that after this, that he lose everything he owns, and that it be at the king's judgment whether he keeps his life.

note.label: extends same penalty
note.quote: For Ine and Alfred, it was a potentially capital crime to draw a weapon in the king's hall. The same penalty now threatened those infringing the royal mund wheresoever

div.note: This term means the violation of anyone’s right of protection over others, but here it is clearly the king’s right which is meant. This is the first occurrence of the term in the laws.
literally, “attack on a homestead”. It includes forcible entry, and injury of persons inside a house. The term is a Scandinavian loan-word and this is its earliest occurrence.
